battle.name: 第一次神聖戰爭
battle.brief: 公元前595年前後，梭倫執政的雅典為帖薩利人出頭，對抗以福基斯人為主的安菲克提翁聯盟，把聯盟武力逐出神廟。事後雅典贏得德爾斐的守護權，並取得安菲克提翁議會的永久主席位。卡面科林斯青銅盔是當時重裝步兵的標準頭盔：窄眼縫、全覆面甲，看不見側翼，於是方陣只能靠盾牌的推力與節奏取勝。

kit.name: 科林斯青銅盔
kit.history: 全正面開眼的青銅盔。看得見的代價是：戴它的人只能靠隊形活。

countries: 第一次神聖戰爭是公元前六世紀上半葉，雅典與德爾斐安菲克提翁聯盟之間的一場短促衝突，通行說法把它的時段放在公元前595年至前585年之間。雅典一方是梭倫改革之後的城邦：全國的重裝步兵（hoplites）按財產等級編戶，能自備盔甲與武器者才有資格服兵役，貴族與阿爾克邁翁家族是改革的受益者，也是支持梭倫的政治力量；軍隊的指揮落在以城邦元老院與五百人議會為核心的制度上，出兵時由一名將軍（strategos）統率，年度將軍選舉制度此時正在成形。對手是德爾斐安菲克提翁聯盟，它不是一個國家，而是十二個族派（ethnē）為管理德爾斐神廟而組成的超城邦機構：福基斯人、玻俄提亞人、多利亞人、洛克里人、馬利安人、佩拉貝人、馬格涅特人、佛提奧特斯的阿開亞人、多洛波斯人與帖薩利諸族各派代表出席，主席（hieromnemon）長期由帖薩利人擔任，議會一年兩度在德爾斐與德摩比利海峽北端的安忒拉開會，擁有制裁違規者的權力，違者可被課以罰款、逐出神域，甚至被判沒收土地。雙方的實力並不對稱：聯盟名義上涵蓋中部希臘廣大土地，卻是鬆散的多國聯盟，軍隊由各城邦臨時徵召，行動遲緩、指揮不統一；雅典則是單一城邦，編制嚴整，士氣與指揮效率較高。另有第三種說法認為開戰的真正對象是美加拉：美加拉在科林斯地峽與雅典爭奪田界，兩國都覬覦德爾斐的影響力，戰爭因此同時是一場地峽走廊的邊界戰爭。
countriesEn: The First Sacred War was a short conflict in the first half of the sixth century BC between Athens and the Delphic Amphictyonic League, conventionally placed between 595 and 585 BC. On the Athenian side stood the polis as it stood after Solon's reforms: the heavy infantry, the hoplites, were enrolled by property class, and only those able to equip themselves with armour and weapons were liable to serve; the aristocracy and the Alcmaeonid family were the beneficiaries of the reform and the political support behind Solon. Command rested on institutions centred on the council of elders and the council of five hundred, with a single strategos commanding a sortie, while the annual election of generals was still taking shape. The opponent was the Delphic Amphictyonic League, which was not a state at all but a supra-political body of twelve peoples, the ethnē, assembled to administer the sanctuary of Delphi. Representatives came from the Phocians, the Boeotians, the Dorians, the Locrians, the Malians, the Perrhaebes, the Magnetes, the Achaeans of Phthiotis, the Dolopians and the Thessalian tribes; the presidency, the hieromnemon, was held for long periods by the Thessalians; the council met twice a year, at Delphi and at Anthela at the northern end of the Thermopylae pass, and it held the power to punish violators, whether by fines, by expulsion from the sacred precinct or by confiscation of land. The two sides were not matched in strength. The league nominally covered a wide area of central Greece, but it was a loose confederation of many cities whose troops were levied ad hoc, slow to move and hard to command; Athens was a single polis, tightly organised, with better discipline and a more efficient command. A third line of interpretation holds that the real object of the war was Megara: Megara and Athens were disputing fields in the Isthmus, and both coveted Delphi's influence, so the war was at the same time a border war over the corridor of the Isthmus.
people: 留下姓名的只有一方，而且不是靠戰場記錄留下來的。梭倫（Solon）是這場戰爭在雅典的化身：他在前594/3年出任執政官（archon），此前已完成取消債務、分區、改革陪審法庭與財產分級等一整套變革；後世把這場戰爭的勝利歸到他的名下，他本人則用一首凱歌（epinician ode）紀念，殘存的兩行詩句保存在亞里斯多德《蛙》的古註裡，說的是雅典人贏得了在神聖地界上的爭鬥——這是關於此戰唯一的一手文字材料。梭倫的私人關係網同樣重要：他與美加拉的希西亞斯（Ἱσσίας）是舊交，而美加拉人涅伊德（Neiðes）在一次安菲克提翁會議上控告福基斯人把神廟周邊土地據為己有、掠取祭祀收入，議會因此判福基斯人罰款，這一事件常被學者排在戰爭前夕，說明開火之前神廟的「地權」糾紛已經公開化。雅典內部支持梭倫的力量包括阿爾克邁翁家族（Alcmaeonidae）與各區的中小自耕農，改革後的城邦第一次以集體的名義在泛希臘舞台上有動作。反過來說，聯盟與帖薩利方面的指揮者姓名都不見於現存文獻；安菲克提翁的軍事指揮由主席與各城邦的將領分擔，帖薩利人提供騎兵，戰役的實際策劃者無從考證，學界只能從事後的政治安排倒推。第四世紀的政治家則反覆把這場戰爭拿來用：德摩斯提尼在《第三斐力普斯》裡說，雅典因為在聖地之爭中幫了帖薩利人，議會把神域的領導權永久判給雅典；伊索克拉底在《演說家理想篇》裡也援引同一件事，作為雅典功績與制度的證明。亞里斯多德《騎士》裡，被指責的民眾領袖被說成敗壞了安菲克提翁人與其他族群，說明這場戰爭在五世紀末仍是雅典人熟悉的政治籌碼。
peopleEn: Only one side left names behind, and not through any record of the battlefield. Solon is the Athenian face of this war: he was archon in 594/3 BC, having already carried out a whole programme of reform, the cancellation of debts, the division of Attica into tribes, the reform of the courts and the grading of citizens by property. Later tradition assigned the victory of the war to him, and he himself marked it in an epinician ode, of which two lines survive in a scholion to Aristophanes' Wasps and which speak of the Athenians winning the dispute over the sacred precinct. That is the only first-hand literary evidence for the war. Solon's private network of contacts mattered as much: he was an old friend of Hissias of Megara, and Neides of Megara had brought before an Amphictyonic council a complaint that the Phocians were treating the land around the temple as their own and were taking the revenue of the sacrifices, so that the council fined the Phocians; scholars usually set this episode immediately before the war, which shows that the quarrel over the land of the sanctuary had already become public. Inside Athens the force behind Solon included the Alcmaeonid family and the middling landowners of the tribes, and the reformed polis was for the first time acting in the Panhellenic arena in its own collective name. On the other side, no name of a commander from the league or from Thessaly survives in the literature. Military command in the Amphictyony was divided between the president and the generals of the individual cities, with the Thessalians providing cavalry, and the actual planner of the campaign cannot be recovered; scholars can only work backwards from the political arrangements made afterwards. Fourth-century politicians used the war repeatedly. Demosthenes, in the Third Philippic, says that because the Athenians had helped the Thessalians in the dispute over the sacred places, the council assigned the leadership of them to the Athenians in perpetuity. Isocrates, in the Areopagiticus, cites the same deed as proof of Athenian merit and of the soundness of her institutions. In Aristophanes' Knights the demagogue accused of perverting the people is charged with having corrupted the Amphictyons among others, which shows that the war was still a familiar political countershot in the late fifth century.
kits: 卡面這頂科林斯青銅盔（Corinthian helmet，考古學上稱「A 型」）正是這場戰爭裡交戰雙方重裝步兵的標準頭盔，年代約前750年至前5世紀中葉，恰好覆蓋前595年這個時點。它的形制是全覆面：頭盔罩住後腦與兩頰，頰甲向下延伸成口鼻護甲，眼部只留兩道狹長的開口，寬度不足以讓戴盔者看清自己的左右兩側。代價與好處同樣明顯：正面視野極佳，擋得住矢石與刀砍，但側向幾近失明，戴盔者只能靠身邊同袍的盾牌與旗幟判斷自己的位置——這正是裝備說明裡所說「只能靠隊形活」的技術原因。與它配套的是hoplon圓盾：直徑約九十厘米的木胎盾，面覆青銅皮，內側有把手與腕帶構成的雙握把，盾緣重得足以承受對撞；希羅多德說阿爾戈斯式的青銅盾重五百至六百達拉姆，約合七點五至九公斤。再配上青銅胸甲（科林斯與阿爾戈斯式的「鐘形」護胸，奧林匹亞出土有例）、皮革或亞麻的護裙、青銅或皮革脛甲，一整套重裝的負重常被估為二十至三十公斤，其中頭盔本身依復原模型約三點五至四點五公斤。矛則是重裝步兵真正用來捅刺的兵器：榆木桿約兩米，裝有套筒式青銅矛頭，尾端有鐏可插地支撐；劍（xiphos）只在較富裕者手上，弓手仍是民兵，攻城器械與大型工程器材在這場衝突裡沒有位置——爭的是神廟的管轄權與地界，不是城牆。交通方面，軍隊靠步行與牛車運糧，前6世紀的希臘重裝步兵作戰仍帶有車隊習慣，戰車已退居將領的座騎與榮耀象徵。值得注意的是頭盔本身的演化：前6世紀中期起，眼孔逐漸放寬、鼻甲縮短、頰甲不再封口的過渡型（B 型、C 型）開始出現，進而在前480年代演成視野更開闊的「阿提卡盔」；換言之，第一次神聖戰爭正好站在科林斯盔與阿提卡盔的交界上，前者是全封閉陣形的最後一代頭盔。
kitsEn: The Corinthian helmet on the card is exactly the standard headgear of the heavy infantry on both sides in this war. Archaeologically it is the type A helmet, in use from about 750 BC to the middle of the fifth century, which brackets the year 595 BC exactly. Its form is one of total enclosure: the helmet covers the back of the head and the cheeks, the cheek pieces run down into a nasal that closes the face, and the eyes are left with only two narrow slits, too narrow for the wearer to see to his own left and right. The cost and the benefit are equally plain. Forward vision is excellent and the face is protected from arrows and blades, but vision sideways is very nearly gone, and the man in the helmet can only judge his place by the shields and standards of the men beside him. That is the technical content of the claim in the equipment note that the wearer can survive only by the formation. Its companion was the hoplon, the round shield: a wooden shield faced with bronze, about ninety centimetres across, with a handle and a forearm grip forming a double grasp along its inner face, and a rim heavy enough to take the shock of two shields pressed together. Herodotus says the Argive bronze shield weighed five hundred to six hundred drachmas, roughly seven and a half to nine kilograms. Add a bronze corselet of the Corinthian and Argive bell shape, of which examples have been found at Olympia, a skirt of leather or linen strips, greaves of bronze or leather, and the whole heavy outfit is commonly put at twenty to thirty kilograms, of which the helmet itself weighs about three and a half to four and a half kilograms on modern reconstructions. The spear was the weapon the hoplite actually used to stab: an ash shaft of about two metres carrying a socketed bronze head, with a butt-spike that could be planted in the ground for support. The sword, the xiphos, belonged to the richer men; the archers remained militia; and siege engines and heavy engineering had no place in this conflict, for what was fought over was jurisdiction over the sanctuary and its land, not a set of walls. In movement the army marched on foot and drew grain by ox-cart, the sixth-century Greek heavy infantry still keeping to convoy habits, while the war chariot had already shrunk to a commander's mount and an emblem of honour. The evolution of the helmet itself is worth noting: from the middle of the sixth century the eye openings began to widen, the nasal shortened and the cheek pieces stopped closing, transitional types B and C appearing, and by the 480s BC they had developed into the far more open Attic helmet. The First Sacred War thus stands exactly on the boundary between the Corinthian and the Attic helmet, and the Corinthian is the last generation of helmets built for a wholly enclosed formation.
tactics: 這場戰爭怎麼打，沒有任何一份戰報留下，只能從時代的希臘方陣習慣與地理條件往回推。前6世紀的希臘戰爭主流已經是重裝步兵方陣：士兵肩並肩密排，前排以圓盾抵住敵盾，後排的手從盾緣上方伸過去頂住前一排的背，形成可以整體推動的「牆」；接戰後雙方互相推擠，勝負靠體重、腳跟支撐與地面的附著力，盾牌不能轉向、視線被擋死，這套動作使任何個人都無法獨自作戰，臨陣脫隊等同於把側背交給敵人。最後進攻的慣例是左翼捲向右翼，兵力較強的一翼繞向敵陣弱側，試圖用旋轉把整條戰線帶動；前6世紀的方陣是否已經有系統性的傾斜（epicyclic formation），學界仍有爭議，亞歷山大的「梯形」與底比斯的「楔形」說法都只能作旁證。投射武器在接戰前用來削弱敵陣：弓手與輕裝步兵先射一輪，掩護方陣前進，箭傷造成的缺口會影響重裝步兵的信心。地理上，德爾斐聖域位於帕爾納索斯山西北麓、刻斐索斯河谷的狹窄地帶，祭壇區與神廟群集中在高處台地，道路只容單列通行；安忒拉一端更窄，位於德摩比利海峽北端的溫泉關入口，聯盟議會在這裡開會本身就是利用了瓶頸地形。補給是最大的弱點：從雅典出發，陸路要經美加拉、科林斯地峽、革拉奈亞山口、埃拉提亞，再沿刻斐索斯河谷北上到安菲施，最後翻山進入德爾斐谷地，全程約一百六十公里，一支重裝步兵師沿途靠各城邦徵收或就地徵用糧食，行軍縱隊拉得極長，幾乎沒有類似後世斯巴達那樣嚴格的糧秣制度。這條走廊在後來兩千年裡被反覆使用：前356年的第三次聖戰、亞歷山大大帝的戰役、公元前279年高盧人進攻德爾菲，走的都是這條線。戰後的裁決也不靠戰場，而靠安菲克提翁議會的程序：勝者把爭議提交議會，議會判對方罰款、要求歸還掠取的神廟財物，並把主席權授予勝方作為酬謝。
tacticsEn: No report of the fighting survives, so the way it was fought can only be reconstructed backwards from the habits of the Greek phalanx in the period and from the geography. The mainstream of Greek warfare in the sixth century BC was already the heavy infantry phalanx: men stood shoulder to shoulder in close order, the front rank bracing round shields against enemy shields, the hands of the ranks behind reaching over the shield rims to press on the backs of the men in front, forming a wall that could be pushed as a whole. Once engaged, the two sides shoved against one another and the outcome turned on weight, the bracing of the heel and the grip of feet on the ground; shields cannot be turned and sight is blocked, and these conditions mean that no individual can fight alone, so leaving the ranks is the same as offering an unprotected flank to the enemy. The custom of the final attack was for the left wing to roll towards the right, the stronger wing working round the weak side of the enemy line in the effort to drag the whole battle line round with it. Whether the sixth-century phalanx already had a systematic refinement, the epicyclic formation, is still disputed, and the stories of the Macedonian echelon and the Theban wedge can only serve as indirect evidence. Missiles were used before contact to weaken the enemy: archers and light troops shot a first round while covering the advance of the phalanx, and the gaps left by arrow wounds affected the confidence of the heavy infantry. Geographically, the sanctuary of Delphi lies in the narrow country of the Cephissus valley on the northwestern slope of Parnassus, with the altar precinct and the temples crowded on a high terrace reachable only by single file; the far end at Anthela is narrower still, at the entrance of Thermopylae at the northern head of the pass, and the fact that the council of the league met there was itself an exploitation of the bottleneck. Supply was the greatest weakness. Marching from Athens by land, the route ran through Megara, the Isthmus, the pass of Geraneia and Elatea, then north along the valley of the Cephissus to Amphissa, and finally over the mountains into the valley of Delphi, some one hundred and sixty kilometres in all; a division of hoplites drew grain on the way by collection from the cities or by requisition on the spot, and the column of march was extremely long, with nothing resembling the strict commissariat of later Sparta. That corridor was used again and again over the following two millennia: the Third Sacred War of 356 BC, the campaigns of Alexander, and the Gallic attack on Delphi in 279 BC all came along it. The verdict after the war was not reached on the battlefield either but through the procedure of the Amphictyonic council: the victor submitted the dispute to the council, which fined the other side, ordered the return of property taken from the sanctuary, and granted the presidency to the winner as a reward.
data: 可核對的數字不多，而且多數屬於推估一類。年代：通行說法是公元前595年至前585年之間的一場「十年期」戰爭；把它繫於梭倫執政年（前594/3年）的做法最流行，另有學者定在前594年或前585/4年；由於唯一的一手材料只是梭倫凱歌的兩行殘句，確切年份無法確定，這份檔案把開戰月份暫記為七月，是依梭倫執政年落在夏季、而泛雅典凱歌通常在大型節慶（潘納忒奈亞在赫卡通巴昂月，約今七月）慶祝的習慣推定的，並非文獻記載。安菲克提翁聯盟的編制數字相對清楚：十二個族派各派代表，議會一年兩度召開，主席由帖薩利人擔任；前586/5年聯盟把德爾斐的皮提奧斯賽會改組為五年一屆的「達耶托斯」（daiétos）制度，是這套機構仍在運作的旁證。兵力方面，兩軍的具體人數都無記載；可以作為標尺的是雅典的hoplite普查數：最早一份完整數字見於《雅典政制》2.37，記錄前460/59年雅典有九千名hoplites，修昔底德2.13則說前431年阿提卡有hoplites三萬名；按此往前推，前6世紀中葉雅典能出動的重裝步兵當在數千人量級，遠不足以與任何聯盟的總量相比，這正是雅典必須靠選擇性介入取勝的原因。裝備數字方面，現代復原模型的估計是科林斯型頭盔約三點五至四點五公斤，hoplon圓盾直徑約九十厘米、重約七至九公斤（希羅多德7.61稱阿爾戈斯式青銅盾重五百至六百達拉姆），全套重裝的總負重常被估為二十至三十公斤，但這個數字因算不算矛與投擲器而異。距離：雅典至德爾斐陸路約一百六十公里，德爾斐聖域台地海拔約六百至七百米，安忒拉則扼住德摩比利海峽北端。考古方面，屬於科林斯盔A型的實物大量出土於奧林匹亞、雅典衛城與科林斯，眼孔放寬的過渡型則集中在前6世紀中葉以後的地層。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked are few, and most of them are estimates. The date: the usual account is a ten-year war between 595 and 585 BC. The most popular way of fixing it is to tie it to Solon's year as archon, 594/3 BC; other scholars choose 594 BC or 585/4 BC. Since the only first-hand material is the two lines of Solon's epinician ode, the exact year cannot be settled, and this record enters July for the opening month as an inference from the archonship falling in the summer and from the custom of celebrating epinician odes at the great festivals, the Panathenaia falling in Hekatombaion, roughly July in our calendar; it is not a documentary date. The organisation of the Amphictyonic League is comparatively clear: representatives of twelve peoples, a council sitting twice a year, the presidency held by the Thessalians. That the machinery was still working is shown by the reorganisation in 586/5 BC of the Pythian games at Delphi into a five-year cycle of daiétos. On numbers of men, nothing is recorded for either army. A usable yardstick is the Athenian hoplite census: the earliest complete figure is in the Athenaion Politeia 2.37, giving nine thousand hoplites for Athens in 460/59 BC, while Thucydides 2.13 says Attica had thirty thousand hoplites in 431 BC. Working backwards from these, the heavy infantry Athens could put in the field in the middle of the sixth century must have been a matter of thousands, far too few to match the total of any coalition, which is precisely why Athens had to win by selective intervention. On equipment, modern reconstructions give the Corinthian-type helmet at about three and a half to four and a half kilograms, and the hoplon at about ninety centimetres across and seven to nine kilograms, Herodotus 7.61 giving five hundred to six hundred drachmas for the Argive bronze shield. The total weight of a full panoply is commonly put at twenty to thirty kilograms, though the figure varies with whether the spear and javelins are counted. On distance, the land route from Athens to Delphi is about one hundred and sixty kilometres, the terrace of the sanctuary at Delphi stands at some six to seven hundred metres above sea level, and Anthela commands the northern head of the Thermopylae pass. In archaeology, examples of the type A Corinthian helmet have come up in quantity at Olympia, on the Athenian Acropolis and at Corinth, while the transitional types with wider eye openings are concentrated in levels of the middle of the sixth century BC and later.
cause: 打起來的原因是三層疊在一起的。第一層是神廟本身的經濟與地權：德爾斐的祭壇周圍早已有被開墾、被分配的土地，神廟的祭祀收入與這些土地的租金構成安菲克提翁聯盟內部的敏感分配；福基斯人長期住在神域一帶、靠神廟維生，被視為既得利益者，美加拉人涅伊德在議會上的控告（神廟土地被某些人據為己有並掠取祭祀收入）就是這條爭端的具體形態，議會判福基斯人罰款，等於承認神廟土地本身可以被立法處置。第二層是聯盟的權威不足：安菲克提翁議會的制裁需要有人執行，而十二個族派各有各的算盤，聯盟既沒有常備軍，也沒有真正的執行力量，一旦神廟被某一方長期佔據，議會就只能借外力。第三層是雅典的介入動機：梭倫改革後的雅典剛在政治上站穩，需要一次能證明城邦行動力的外部勝利；雅典在科林斯地峽一帶與美加拉長期爭奪地界（阿提卡在科林斯地峽東岸的殖民地索利翁在前6世紀落入美加拉之手），而德爾斐正卡在通往北方的大道上，掌握神廟就等於掌握走廊的主導權。於是有了第三種流行解釋：所謂「第一次神聖戰爭」的實質，是雅典與美加拉為科林斯地峽田界而起的衝突，德爾斐只是被援引的公義理由，其依據是伊斯特米亞出土的地界碑銘文，碑上提到美加拉人侵奪阿提卡境內的神聖地界。學界至今分成兩派：一派以梭倫凱歌與安菲克提翁的司法權為中心，認定這是一場為神域而打的仲裁戰爭；另一派以地界碑與雅典的戰略利益為中心，認定它是一場被神聖外衣包裝的邊界戰爭。比較穩妥的說法是：兩種動機並存，且不矛盾。
causeEn: The reasons for fighting lie in three layers, laid one on another. The first is the economy and the land of the sanctuary itself. The ground around the altar of Delphi had long been brought under cultivation and allotted, and the revenue of the sacrifices together with the rents of those plots made up a sensitive distribution inside the Amphictyonic League. The Phocians, who had lived for a long time in the sacred district and subsisted on the temple, were treated as men with a vested interest, and the complaint brought by Neides of Megara in the council, that certain men were treating the land of the sanctuary as their own and taking the revenue of the sacrifices, is the concrete form of that quarrel. The council's fining of the Phocians amounted to a recognition that the land of the temple itself could be disposed of by legislation. The second layer is the weakness of the league's authority. The sanctions of the Amphictyonic council needed someone to execute them, but each of the twelve peoples had its own arithmetic; the league had no standing army and no real means of enforcement, and once the sanctuary was occupied for long by one party, the council could only borrow power from outside. The third layer is the motive for Athenian intervention. The reformed Athens had only just established itself politically and needed an external success that would demonstrate the capacity of the polis to act; Athens and Megara had been disputing fields in the Isthmus for a long time, the Attic colony of Soly on the eastern side of the Isthmus having fallen to Megara in the sixth century, and Delphi stood on the great road to the north, so that control of the sanctuary was control of the corridor. Hence the third and popular interpretation: the substance of the so-called First Sacred War was a quarrel between Athens and Megara over fields in the Isthmus, with Delphi serving as the borrowed plea of right, a reading resting on the boundary inscription found at Isthmia, which records the seizure by Megarians of sacred land within Attic territory. Scholarship remains divided: one school, taking the ode of Solon and the jurisdiction of the Amphictyony as its centre, holds that this was an arbitral war fought for the sanctuary; the other, taking the boundary stone and the strategic interests of Athens as its centre, holds that it was a border war wrapped in a sacred cloak. The safer account is that both motives were present and are not incompatible.
impact: 這場戰爭的後果，主要是象徵性的，也是長期的。第一，雅典得到了一件可以反覆支取的資產：德爾斐的守護權與安菲克提翁議會的主席位（hieromnemonia）。到前四世紀，雅典仍在援引這項權利，德摩斯提尼與伊索克拉底都把它寫成雅典對泛希臘世界有功的證明，說明它不是一次性的戰利品，而是一份帶著判決書的長期權力。第二，這讓雅典的戰略位置大為改觀：控制德爾斐與安忒拉，等於握住了由科林斯地峽通向北方的走廊咽喉，往後腓力二世、斯巴達的 Agesilaus、埃托利亞人、高盧人與羅馬人都要在這條線上爭奪同一個節點，這條線的戰略價值從前6世紀起就被確立。第三，泛希臘的「以神廟仲裁」觀念獲得一次成功的示範：在一個沒有常設國際軍隊的世界裡，一場由神廟產權引起的衝突，最後仍回到神廟的議會裡解決，並且勝方用一份永久的主席權作為賠償；這套邏輯在後世被不斷援引，近代國際法與國際仲裁的論述裡，它是最常被拿來做古典先例的案例之一。第四，神廟本身成為雅典與聯盟共同經營的資產：前6世紀末德爾斐進行了重建，德爾斐阿爾克邁翁人建築群常被繫於這個時期，年代仍有爭議；前586/5年聯盟把皮提奧斯賽會改組為五年一屆，也讓德爾斐的節慶體系更制度化。第五，這場戰爭在後世的政治論述中幾乎被工具化：只要有人要為雅典干預鄰邦辯護，就可以援引「雅典人曾為別人打過仗」；反過來，它也成了「藉口」與「真相」之辯的經典教材。考古上，戰場本身沒有留下可辨的戰鬥遺址，戰爭的痕跡更多留在文獻殘篇、銘文與神廟沿革裡。
impactEn: The consequences of this war were chiefly symbolic, and they were long-lived. First, Athens acquired an asset that could be drawn on repeatedly: the guardianship of Delphi and the presidency of the Amphictyonic council, the hieromnemonia. By the fourth century BC Athens was still claiming that right, and both Demosthenes and Isocrates set it down as proof of what Athens had done for the Panhellenic world, which shows that it was not a one-off prize but a durable power backed by a formal ruling. Second, it transformed the strategic position of Athens: control of Delphi and Anthela meant a hand on the throat of the corridor running north from the Isthmus, and after that Philip II, the Spartan Agesilaus, the Aetolians, the Gauls and the Romans were all to contest the same node on the same line, so that the strategic value of that corridor was settled from the sixth century BC onward. Third, the Panhellenic idea of arbitration through a sanctuary received a successful demonstration: in a world without standing international armies, a conflict begun over the property of a temple was at last settled inside the council of that temple, and the victor was paid in a permanent presidency; the logic was invoked again and again, and in modern argument about international law and international arbitration this war is one of the most frequently used classical precedents. Fourth, the sanctuary itself became an asset held jointly in the interest of Athens and the league: Delphi was rebuilt at the end of the sixth century, the so-called Alcmaeonid buildings at Delphi being commonly attached to that period though the dating is disputed, and the league's reorganisation of the Pythian games into a five-year cycle in 586/5 BC made the festival system of Delphi more institutional. Fifth, the war was almost wholly turned into an instrument of later political argument: whenever anyone wanted to justify Athenian intervention in the affairs of a neighbour, the claim could be made that the Athenians had once fought on behalf of others, and in the other direction it became a standard textbook case of the difference between pretext and truth. Archaeologically the battlefield itself has left no identifiable remains of the fighting; the traces of the war survive in fragments of literature, in inscriptions and in the history of the sanctuary.
result: 結局在文獻上只有一句話：雅典人贏了。按第四世紀雅典人的說法，安菲克提翁議會對這場神聖地界的爭議作出裁決，把神域的領導權永久地判給雅典，雅典從此自居為德爾斐的守護者，直到前四世紀仍在援引這項權利；德爾斐的皮提亞所代表的雅典影響力，在前5世紀前半達到高點，雅典也把自己寫進了泛希臘的宗教秩序裡，成為潘那托斯與皮提奧斯等節慶的守護者之一。對安菲克提翁聯盟來說，結果恰恰相反：聯盟第一次證明自己在真正的武力衝突中無力執行制裁，神廟的仲裁權被外來大國的保護權架空，議會此後的每一次「神聖處分」都更依賴雅典、斯巴達、底比斯與馬其頓這些城邦去執行——前449/8年的第二次聖戰、腓力二世引發的前356至前346年的第三次聖戰，都是這同一個結構的重演，直到前3世紀埃托利亞聯盟接管德爾斐與議會，這個以神廟為名的超城邦機構才真正退場。必須坦白的是，這場戰爭的具體經過幾乎無可靠記載：交戰日期、交戰地點、雙方兵力、戰術細節都無從查證，唯一的直接線索是梭倫凱歌的兩行殘句，其餘全是從制度、地理與後世政治用途所作的重建；因此這份檔案中的月份、地點與戰役經過帶有推定性質，可以確定的是它的名字、它的性質（第一次以神廟產權為名的希臘城邦戰爭），以及它留在希臘人記憶裡的那個位置。
resultEn: The outcome is one sentence in the literature: the Athenians won. On the account given in the fourth century BC, the Amphictyonic council gave its verdict on the dispute over the sacred precincts and assigned the leadership of the sacred places to the Athenians in perpetuity; from then on Athens described itself as the guardian of Delphi, and was still claiming that right in the fourth century BC. The influence represented at Delphi by the Pythia reached its height in the first half of the fifth century, and Athens wrote itself into the Panhellenic religious order as one of the guardians of festivals such as the Panathenaia and the Pythian games. For the Amphictyonic League the result was exactly the opposite. The league had proved for the first time that it lacked the means to execute its own sanctions in a real clash of arms, the jurisdiction of the sanctuary was hollowed out by the protective power of outside states, and every subsequent sacred penalty of the council came to depend more and more on Athens, Sparta, Thebes and Macedon to carry it out. The Second Sacred War of 449/8 BC and the Third Sacred War of 356 to 346 BC, which ran under Philip II, are both rehearsals of that same structure, and only when the Aetolian League took over Delphi and the council in the third century BC did this supra-political body named after a temple finally leave the stage. It must be admitted that almost nothing reliable survives about how the war was actually fought: the dates, the place, the numbers on both sides and the tactical details cannot be verified, and the only direct thread is the two lines of Solon's epinician ode, everything else being reconstruction from institutions, geography and the political use made of the war in later times. The month, the place and the course of the battle in this record therefore carry an element of reconstruction; what can be settled is its name, its character as the first Greek polis war fought over the property of a sanctuary, and the place it kept in Greek memory.
